## Standards

**Findings: 3. Worst: hard violation—cleanup failures are silently discarded.**

1. **Hard — `src/recorder/run.ts:47-52` — failure dishonesty.**  
   The changed hunk defines cleanup as:
   > `try { rmSync(...) } catch {}`  
   and `fail()` proceeds normally after calling it. This violates `CLAUDE.md`, **失败诚实宪法**: “真因必须落痕；catch 后照常继续视同缺陷，除非「此失败下继续」是文档化契约。” No documented cleanup-failure continuation contract was found. (`dist/recorder/run.js` mirrors the shipped violation.)

2. **Judgment — `src/recorder/extract.ts:164-169` — Middle Man / Speculative Generality.**  
   The added “Compatibility entry point” merely constructs `AcceptanceCollector`, forwards every row to `accept`, then calls `finish`. It is used only by the new tests, while production directly uses `AcceptanceCollector`; the ticket expressly replaces rather than preserves the old core. This compatibility wrapper is an unnecessary delegating abstraction:
   > `export function extractAcceptedReceipt(rows: unknown[]): ExtractionResult`

3. **Judgment — changed production helpers in `src/recorder/run.ts:47-92` — Mysterious Name.**  
   Newly introduced names `p`, `c`, `s`, `e`, `dest`, and `err` obscure path/config/settlement/error roles, notably:
   > `const cleanup = (p: string | null)`  
   > `function destination(c: ...)`  
   > `function outcome(s: ...)`  
   The baseline requires names to reveal what values hold. The same generated names appear in `dist/recorder/run.js`; counted as one source-level smell, not duplication.

No missing, partial, wrong, or scope-creep behavior found at pinned target `361f2684e3a0e4bc06cd96ddfce294295cf2a45a`.

Summary: Standards—3 findings; worst is the hard failure-dishonesty violation from silently discarded cleanup failures. Spec—0 findings; no issue.
